Hi Rishi / Jasmine,

Thanks for sending over the blank MSA and Order Form during the demo last week. Attached is our procurement redline (FinServ_MSA_redline_v2.docx). Two items surfaced in our legal review that I want to flag up front so we can get clarity before routing for signatures:

1) Regulatory fines / statutory penalties (GDPR / CCPA / PCI): our counsel insists that any party responsible for regulatory penalties resulting from a data breach or non-compliance should remain fully liable to the extent caused by that party's acts or omissions. They are pushing for an explicit carve-out from any overall limitation of liability.

2) Third-party claims tied to PCI / payment card breaches: we need clarity on whether third-party suits (card networks, acquirers) are treated as indemnified claims (defense + indemnity) or fall within a capped direct-liability bucket.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: (a) whether regulatory fines will be carved out from the cap, and (b) whether Redwood will indemnify FinServ for third-party PCI claims caused by Redwood? If you can provide proposed redline language, that will speed things up.

Attached: FinServ_MSA_redline_v2.docx (redline), SOC2_Summary_2025.pdf (requested by our security team).

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is aiming to complete legal by end of next week.

Elena —

Thanks for the redline and the flags. We reviewed with Legal and Security. High level: Redwood's standard approach is to have an overall cap tied to fees paid under the Order Form (12 months of fees for SaaS), with certain carve-outs for gross negligence and willful misconduct. For regulatory fines and third-party claims, we think a narrow, risk-balanced compromise will be the fastest path to execution.

Proposed approach (summary):
- Regulatory fines/penalties: Redwood is prepared to accept responsibility for regulatory fines to the extent they result directly from Redwood's breach of its data protection obligations or willful misconduct. For fines arising from the customer's environment/configuration or customer-controlled data handling, liability should remain with FinServ. We do not propose an uncapped blanket carve-out.
- Third-party PCI claims: Redwood can agree to indemnify for third-party claims tied to Redwood's negligence or security failings (including PCI scope issues caused by Redwood), subject to a sub-cap equal to 24 months of Order Form fees for that product and standard indemnity procedures (tendered defense, cooperation).

Neha has drafted proposed redline text — she is cc'd. If that language looks acceptable, we'll incorporate it into a clean copy and return. If FinServ prefers unconstrained liability for regulatory penalties, that will have pricing and insurance implications we should discuss (likely additional contractual insurance and an elevated SOW).

I'll wait for Neha's text and keep the thread moving.

Thanks,

Subject: Draft redline language: Limitation of Liability — regulatory penalties / third-party claims

Elena / Rishi —

Below is the proposed contract language from Redwood Legal. It is intentionally specific to address FinServ's concern while preserving our unit economics and insurance boundaries. Please review and tell me if you want this sent in tracked changes in the MSA docx or added as a short addendum.

Proposed additions / edits (MSA §9 — Limitation of Liability):
"Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the aggregate liability of Supplier (Redwood Inference) to Customer for all claims arising out of or related to this Agreement shall not exceed the total Fees paid by Customer to Supplier under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) month period preceding the event giving rise to the claim; provided, however, that the foregoing limitation shall not apply to (i) liability for death or personal injury resulting from Supplier's gross negligence or willful misconduct; (ii) Supplier's liability for amounts that Supplier is required to pay pursuant to a final judgment for intellectual property infringement; and (iii) Supplier's liability for regulatory fines and statutory penalties to the extent such fines and penalties arise directly from Supplier's (A) willful misconduct, or (B) material breach of Supplier's data protection obligations under Section X (Data Protection and Security)."

"Supplier shall indemnify and defend Customer from and against any third-party claims (including claims by payment card networks or acquirers) to the extent such claims arise directly from Supplier's gross negligence or failure to comply with Supplier's obligations with respect to PCI applicable to the Services; provided that Supplier's indemnity for such third-party claims shall be subject to a sub-cap equal to twenty-four (24) months of Fees billed under the applicable Order Form and shall be subject to the indemnity procedures set forth in Section Y."

Notes / rationale: these edits (a) make regulatory fines a carve-out only where Redwood is at fault (willful misconduct or material data protection breach), (b) provide a committed indemnity for third-party PCI claims but with a defined sub-cap and standard procedural protections, and (c) avoid exposing Redwood to unlimited uncapped exposure for events outside our control.

Impact: if FinServ needs an uncapped exposure for regulatory fines irrespective of cause, we will need to discuss additional insurance (cyber liability), a higher unit price, or a specific SOW/escrow for high-risk data flows.

If you sign off, I will produce a tracked-changes MSA and a clean copy for signature.
